sections.h2: Where is Fayette County and what does the land look like?
sections.html:
Fayette County is in south-central West Virginia, just north of Beckley, with Fayetteville as the county seat. It covers about 668 square miles of high plateau, bordered by Sewell Mountain on the east and the Kanawha Valley on the west. The New River cuts a deep gorge through the middle and joins the Gauley at Gauley Bridge to form the Kanawha, according to the West Virginia Encyclopedia.

Neighbors are Nicholas, Greenbrier, Summers, Raleigh and Kanawha counties. The West Virginia Turnpike (Interstates 64 and 77) crosses the western part, and U.S. 19 crosses the New River Gorge Bridge, which the encyclopedia calls the county's chief landmark. Other routes include U.S. 60 and state routes 16, 39, 41 and 61.

The county's incorporated places are Fayetteville, Oak Hill, Mount Hope, Ansted, Gauley Bridge, Meadow Bridge, Pax and Thurmond, with Montgomery and Smithers shared with other counties. Local government uses three magisterial districts: New Haven, Plateau and Valley. A parcel on the plateau and a parcel in a river town can sit in different districts, so the district name on the tax ticket is worth knowing.

sections.h2: How did Fayette County's history shape its housing?
sections.html:
Coal and the railroad built most of Fayette County's older towns, and the decline of coal emptied some of them. The Chesapeake and Ohio Railway finished its line through the New River Gorge on January 29, 1873, and the county's population grew from 6,647 in 1870 to 60,377 in 1920. It peaked at 82,443 in 1950, then fell as mines closed.

The encyclopedia says the gorge, once crowded with mining towns, is now almost empty of residents, and that road building pulled the county away from the river and rail line onto the plateau. The 2025 estimate is 38,165 people, down 5.8 percent from the 2020 count.

That history leaves a county where population has dropped for decades, yet where visitors keep arriving. Sellers here are often dealing with a house in a small town, a lot outside any municipality, or an inherited property whose owners live out of state. Each of those leads to the same practical question: who pays the tax ticket until the deed changes hands.

sections.h2: What does the Fayette County economy rely on now?
sections.html:
Outdoor tourism is the county's growth story, and the New River Gorge National Park and Preserve anchors it. The National Park Service reports 1,811,937 recreation visits in 2024, with visitors spending an estimated $95.5 million in the surrounding region, which supported 948 jobs. The park was redesignated in December 2020, and whitewater rafting on the New and Gauley rivers, rock climbing, biking and fishing bring visitors.

The same encyclopedia entry for West Virginia's economy lists Fayette among the counties classified as persistent poverty areas, meaning rates above 20 percent for at least three decades.

sections.h2: Where and how do you pay Fayette County property tax?
sections.html:
You pay the Fayette County Sheriff's Tax Office, which is open 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., Monday through Friday. The county's tax department page gives these details.

  • Office: 100 Church Street, Fayetteville. Enter through the Church Street and Magistrate Court entrance, because the East Maple Avenue doors do not open into the tax or assessor offices.
  • Drop box: located by the East Maple Avenue tax door.
  • By mail: Sheriff of Fayette County, P.O. Box 509, Fayetteville, WV 25840. Include a stamped, self-addressed envelope for the receipt.
  • Phone: 304-574-4219.
  • Online: through the sheriff's search and payment site. Credit card payments carry a processing fee.

Postmarks count as the time of payment. The page also states the discount and penalty rules in plain terms.

sections.h2: What are the Fayette County property tax deadlines and penalties?
sections.html:
The first half is due September 1 and the second half March 1, and each earns a 2.5 percent discount if paid on or before that date. Nine percent annual interest starts when a half becomes delinquent, which is October 1 for the first half and April 1 for the second, as the state due dates page confirms.

Fayette adds a local warning: taxes still unpaid on April 30 are subject to publication, and publication brings extra fees. The county tells owners to contact the office for cut-off dates on delinquent properties.

State law then runs a clock. Section 11A-3-2 has the sheriff prepare a second list of delinquent land by September 10. Liens still unredeemed are certified to the State Auditor on October 31 and sold at public auction for at least the taxes, interest and charges. A person can redeem before certification by paying the sheriff, and after certification by paying the Auditor, any time before the sale.

sections.h2: How much of Fayette County's tax goes to schools?
sections.html:
Schools receive about 62 percent of what Fayette County levies, based on the state's report for the 2024 tax year. The table shows the amounts levied on all property that year.

PurposeTaxes levied, 2024 tax year
State$139,827
County$11,997,163
Schools$23,686,712

Total$38,212,321

The same Tax Division report splits the total by property class: $9,570,546 on Class II owner-occupied homes and farms, $19,970,745 on Class III property outside municipalities and $8,671,030 on Class IV property inside them. Class III carries more than half the burden, which is consistent with a county that has a lot of land outside towns. The percentage for schools is my own division of the report's figures.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Fayette County assessment?
sections.html:
Challenge it before the County Commission acting as the Board of Equalization and Review, which meets starting February 1. Property is assessed as of July 1 at 60 percent of true and actual value under section 11-3-1, so a challenge is really an argument about what the house would have sold for on that date.

The board can adjourn after February 15 and must adjourn by the end of February. An owner who never applies at that meeting cannot revisit the list for that year except by appeal to the Office of Tax Appeals, and the deadline for that appeal is March 31. Anyone facing a higher value gets at least five days of written notice and a chance to speak, under section 11-3-24. The assessor's office at 100 Church Street handles real estate questions at 304-574-4239 or 304-574-4240.

sections.h2: Is there a homestead exemption in Fayette County?
sections.html:
Yes, for owners who are 65 or older or permanently and totally disabled, and it removes the first $20,000 of assessed value. Section 11-6B-3 sets the rule and requires two consecutive calendar years of West Virginia residence. The county tax page says the application period is July 1 through December 1, that it covers a primary residence only, and invites anyone 64 or older to contact the assessor.

A seller who already holds the exemption should say so when a buyer, or a title agent, asks about prorating the year's tax. The statute ties the exemption to the claimant, so a buyer would need to qualify on their own.

sections.h2: What does selling a Fayette County house with taxes due involve?
sections.html:
A title agent pays unpaid taxes from the seller's proceeds, and the deed transfer carries its own tax. Under section 11-22-2, recording a deed costs $1.10 per $500 of value plus a county tax of 55 cents per $500, which the commission may raise to $1.65, and a $20 fee on a transfer for consideration. The grantor pays unless the grantee accepts the deed without payment.

For a $95,700 house, the base rates add up to $1.65 per $500, which comes to about $317 (192 units of $500). That is my arithmetic, and the county may charge more, so check with the clerk.

Time matters most when a parcel is close to April 30 publication or the September list. A cash purchase can close in days and settle the open ticket, which keeps the property off the delinquent list.

sections.h2: Do rental owners in Fayette County owe anything besides property tax?
sections.html:
Fayette County runs a hotel and motel occupancy tax through its tax department. It is due by the 15th of the month after collection, with a $15 late penalty, a 2.5 percent penalty for the first delinquent month and 1.5 percent for each month after. The county's page says no later payment is accepted until earlier delinquencies are paid in full.

Whether a particular house rented to guests counts is a question for the tax department, and a seller who has been renting near the park should ask before closing so no occupancy tax balance is left behind.

faqs.q: Who do I pay property tax to in Fayette County?
faqs.a: The Fayette County Sheriff's Tax Office at 100 Church Street in Fayetteville, or by mail to P.O. Box 509, Fayetteville, WV 25840. The phone number is 304-574-4219, and online payment is available.

faqs.q: When do Fayette County property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: October 1 for the first half and April 1 for the second half. Interest of 9 percent per year then applies, and taxes unpaid on April 30 are subject to publication with added fees.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Fayette County house that has unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The tax balance, plus any interest, is normally paid from your proceeds at closing. Ask the sheriff's office for a current payoff amount before you commit to a date.

faqs.q: How do I apply for the Fayette County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Apply at the Fayette County Assessor's Office between July 1 and December 1. You must be 65 or older, or permanently and totally disabled, and the exemption covers a primary residence only.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal a Fayette County assessment?
faqs.a: Start with the Board of Equalization and Review, which meets from February 1 and finishes by the end of February. Appeals of its decision to the Office of Tax Appeals are due March 31.
